changes: Toolbox discovery exposes eleven lazy local security tools from an inert SHA-pinned wheel.
Official CVE baseline and cumulative delta are mirrored locally with raw record provenance and bounded read-only results.
A covering SQLite index accelerates full state counts without dropping fields or changing logical CVE data.
Supplied source/dependency evidence and bounded Ghidra analysis use fresh current-task ownership and instruction hashes.
Camera startup retires only proven expired-owner workers; new capture families use kill-on-close Windows Jobs.
Unconfirmed camera cleanup retains ownership and prevents replacement; readiness requires a valid frame and fatal errors remain fatal.
Self-checks collect packaged tests and bind actual installed Python, Java and test bytes, not just package versions.

validation.scope: Four full affected validation modules and two existing prompt controls; not the complete application suite.

wheel.verification: Tampered valid ZIP rejected by pip hash check; direct and requirements-file installs into separate owned targets passed. Import origins and nine file hashes matched; no import-time DB/network/process activity.

real_backend_evidence.data_preservation: All typed logical document/batch/active/FTS/ancillary table identities and seven raw CVE samples matched before and after index construction.
real_backend_evidence.ghidra: Known neutral PE64 imported and decompiled to return42 in17.46s; subject was never executed.
real_backend_evidence.camera: A proven expired-owner camera family prevented opening the webcam. Exact orphan retirement restored capture; the installed negotiation routine delivered1920x1080@30fps. No private camera screenshot or frames are included in this evidence.

retained_failures: Original Ghidra exporter compile error and hidden-project-path runtime failure were fixed and retained as diagnostic evidence.
Windows path-anchor and lstat/fstat timestamp mismatches were fixed without weakening raw-byte instruction binding.
Actual catalog status exceeded the SQL budget before the covering index; no budget increase or state-count omission was used.
The scope writer could exceed its reader bound; the new guard rejects oversized scopes before publishing them.
Static camera review caught lost cleanup ownership, pending-child handoff and late-success races before execution.
limits: Not the complete installed application self-check.
Physical-camera recovery and real neutral-PE Ghidra backend were separately verified, not rerun by this CPU suite.
Existing owned Toolbox Python/dependencies reused; exact installer payload qualification still required.
No live client website audit, arbitrary binary verdict or actual-model app-delivery success claim.
CVE/product/version overlaps and source patterns are investigation leads, not confirmed deployed vulnerabilities; absence of matches is not clearance.
Decompilation is approximate and format-dependent. No universal reverse-engineering, arbitrary-binary or live-client-site verdict.
Camera ownership is scoped to known app processes and the current GUI lifetime; unknown legacy owners are preserved, not killed by name.
CVE storage needs several gigabytes. Retention preserves active/partial/unknown data and reuses SQLite pages without automatic VACUUM.
The old updater installs dependencies before source activation; a source rollback does not uninstall the inert wheel.
